messages:
alex: heads-up — customer using python sdk behind a corporate mitm proxy getting `ssl.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed` when calling our api. wondering fastest way to help them debug / workaround.

sam: ugh, classic. do they control the machine? can they provide the full trace + openssl s_client output?

alex: minimal trace pasted below from their app:
```
requests.exceptions.SSLError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='api.redwood.ai', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /v1/generate (Caused by SSLError(SSLCertVerificationError("[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1007)")))
```

jess: quick checklist:
- are they using system python or bundled with macOS? certifi outdated? try `python -c "import certifi; print(certifi.where())"`
- if behind corp mitm, they likely need to add corporate CA to trust bundle or set `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` env var.

maria: exact commands I hand out:
1) dump server cert with openssl: `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect api.redwood.ai:443` and check chain
2) if corp CA present, save it as `corp.pem` and set `export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/corp.pem` for requests-based apps

alex: nice. customer says they can't change env widely (legacy container). any in-code workaround for python sdk we can recommend temporarily?

sam: yes — in requests-based code you can pass `verify='/path/to/corp.pem'` to the underlying session or to `requests.get(...)`. our SDK exposes `client._session` in v0.x? but don't rely on private attrs. we can add a documented `verify` option to our client config in a patch release.

jess: for node users: set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/corp.pem` or supply `ca` to `https.Agent`.

alex: java note: if JVM, add corp cert to a truststore and run with `-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/path/to/truststore.jks` or use PKCS12. also some app servers override default keystore so watch that.

maria: go tip: `x509.SystemCertPool()` on linux might be empty in some distros; load custom pool or point `TLSConfig.RootCAs` to a file.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0427 (customer: ACME Corp) — assigned to devex oncall

sam: longterm: we should add a README section "Using the SDK behind corporate proxies / custom CA" + a small API to pass `ca_bundle` or `verify` so users don't need env hacks. filing a tiny RFC.

jess: +1. also add tests that set `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` in CI to avoid regressions where requests starts using certifi changes.

alex: ok I'll ping product for doc slot and open a PR to add `verify`/`ca_bundle` arg to the python client (backwards compatible). attaching the customer's openssl snip to the incident.

maria: if anyone wants to pair on the PR lmk, I can help with test matrix across py37/py310 and mac/linux. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks all — closing the loop, will update INC when we have the patch.
